title: Childhood funeral parades and hearing Joe Oliver
summary: As a boy he followed funeral parades with marching bands, hearing Joe Oliver, and his parents merely watched with tongue-in-cheek enjoyment.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: Well, my introduction to it was many, many years ago. I don't think I was aware of it as being jazz, nor was it called jazz then, but I had a nice, a Negro nice, who used to take me walking up and down St. Charles Avenue, and occasionally, a mother would let me accompany her to the grocery, which was in the Negro section about five squares away from St. Charles Avenue towards Dryad Street. And it was amazing how she seemed to get by grapevine that every time we went to this grocery, there'd always be a funeral procession with a marching band. And I didn't know what it was all about, but it enthused me very, very much. And I loved to join in a bunch of both whites and Negro children that were following the band along the street. And it happened to be that I was listening to Joe Oliver at that time. That was my introduction to it.
Well, what did your parents think of this whole music? And your parents...
